findings.heading: Sub-graph clusters (Complex examples / Karmaşık örnekler)
findings.proposition: English says the subgraph name must begin with the literal string "cluster"; the Turkish says it must begin with "küme", while the DOT code in the very next chunk (diagrams.tr.qmd:309, 322, 327, 333) uses cluster_passive, cluster_active, cluster_EBD and cluster_CBS.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader who follows the prose and names a subgraph 'kume_passive' gets no bounding box at all, because Graphviz only draws a cluster box when the subgraph name starts with the reserved prefix 'cluster'. The failure is silent: the graph still renders, just without the grouping the section is teaching.

findings.heading: Syntax / Sözdizimi
findings.proposition: English lists the legal values of the node attribute `shape` as ellipse, oval, diamond, egg, plaintext, point, square, triangle; the Turkish lists elips, oval, elmas, yumurta, düz metin, nokta, kare, üçgen, which are not values DOT accepts.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader writing node [shape = elmas] or shape = 'düz metin' produces an invalid DOT attribute; Graphviz falls back to the default ellipse or errors, and the reader has no way to recover the correct keyword from the page.

findings.heading: Syntax / Sözdizimi
findings.proposition: English lists the legal values of the edge attribute `arrowhead` as normal, box, crow, curve, diamond, dot, inv, none, tee, vee; the Turkish lists normal, kutu, karga, eğri, elmas, nokta, inv, yok, tee, vee, which are not values DOT accepts.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader writing arrowhead = yok expecting no arrowhead, or arrowhead = kutu for a box head, gets an unrecognised value and the default arrowhead instead, with no hint on the page that the keyword must stay English.

findings.heading: Syntax / Sözdizimi
findings.proposition: English gives `dashed` as the example value of the edge attribute `style`; the Turkish gives 'kesik çizgili', which is not a DOT style value, and the code chunk beside it at diagrams.tr.qmd:282 uses style = dashed.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader writing style = kesik çizgili gets a solid line and a parse problem, even though the working example three sections earlier in the same file uses style = dashed.

findings.heading: Plotting from dataset / Veri kümesinden grafik yapma
findings.proposition: English says the node data frame holds the values under the column `name`; the Turkish says they are held under `sütun adı`, while the code beside it creates a column literally called name (diagrams.tr.qmd:551-554) and later passes NodeID = "name" to sankeyNetwork() (diagrams.tr.qmd:585).
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader looking for a column called 'sütun adı' cannot connect the prose to the data frame in the chunk, and does not learn why the sankeyNetwork() argument must be NodeID = "name"; adapting the example to their own data they may rename the column and break the plot.

findings.heading: Syntax / Sözdizimi
findings.proposition: The Turkish glosses RL as 'sağdan sola' (right-to-left) and BT as 'aşağıdan yukarıya' (bottom-to-top); the English lists RL and BT with no expansion at all.
findings.reader_consequence: None harmful: the glosses are correct. It is content the English does not carry, so the two versions teach a different amount about rankdir, and a later edit to the English list will not be reflected here.

findings.heading: Parameterized figures / Parametreli şekiller
findings.proposition: The quoted tutorial says the benefit is designing FIGURES (diagrams) inside R and reading R values into the flowcharts; the Turkish renders 'figures' as 'Rakamlar' (numerals/digits), so it states the benefit is designing numbers in R and connecting numbers to the analysis.
findings.reader_consequence: A Turkish reader meets 'Rakamları R içinde tasarlamak' at the start of the quote and cannot tell that the passage is about parameterising a diagram; the section heading uses the correct word 'şekiller', so the two terms conflict inside one section.
